'''Predrag Savović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Предраг Савовић}}; born 21 May 1976) is a Montenegrin former professional [[basketball]] player. Among many teams in his professional career he played for [[KK Partizan|KK Partizan Belgrade]], the [[National Basketball Association]]'s [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[CB Bilbao Berri|Iurbentia Bilbao]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB|ACB]].

==Early life and college career==
[[File:Universityof Hawaii Vs. Fresno State 2001.jpg|left|thumb]]
[[File:523c81f563be4.preview-300.jpg|thumb|WAC Champions 2002, University of Hawaii]]

Savović was born in [[Pula]], [[SR Croatia]], at the time part of [[SFR Yugoslavia]], to a family of [[Montenegrins|Montenegrin]] descent. He attended Ivan Goran Kovačić High School in [[Herceg Novi]], [[Montenegro]]. He attended the [[University of Alabama-Birmingham]] (UAB) from 1997 to 1998 and then the [[University of Hawaii at Manoa]], in the U.S., from 1998 to 2002. He holds degrees in International Business and Finance as well as Economics from the University of Hawaii at Manoa.<ref>[https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/game-center/?clubcode=bil&pcode=CKG EurocupBasketball.com Profile]</ref> He also holds an [[Master of Business Administration|EMBA]] Degree from [[University of Deusto]], Deusto Business School. Predrag was a first-team All-[[Western Athletic Conference]] pick in his junior and senior seasons, the MVP of the 2002 [[WAC men's basketball tournament|WAC tournament]], and an honorable mention All-American selection by the [[Associated Press]]. Hawaii advanced to the first round of the [[2002 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament of 2002]].<ref name="NBA bio">{{cite web|title=Predrag Savovic bio|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/predrag_savovic/bio.html|publisher=NBA|accessdate=9 February 2012|url-status=bot: unknown|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080117080617/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/predrag_savovic/bio.html|archivedate=17 January 2008}}</ref>

==Career==

Savović grew up playing for [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]], [[KK Beovuk 72|Beovuk]], and [[KK Zorka Šabac|IVA Zorka Pharm Šabac]]. He moved to the American [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] even though he was well into his twenties. [[NBA draft|Undrafted]], he signed with the [[National Basketball Association]]'s [[Denver Nuggets]] in 2002, for whom he played during the [[2002-03 NBA season]], making him one of only few European players at guard position by that time that made a transition from NCAA to NBA without being drafted. He only played in 27 NBA games, totaling 83 points, 25 rebounds and 22 assists. Savović' final NBA game was played on April 2, 2003, in a 75 - 83 loss to the [[New York Knicks]] where he played for nearly 5 minutes and had no stats other than three missed field-goals.

For the last five years of his professional basketball career, he has been an important member of [[Bilbao Basket]], a member of [[Liga ACB|ACB League]] in Spain until his retirement in 2009.{{citation needed|date=April 2018}}

==Personal life and business career==
[[File:Predrag Savovic Jovanovic.jpg|thumb|298x298px]]

Predrag Savović is a co-founder of IBEXMONT D.O.O:, a consulting firm based in [[Montenegro|Republic of Montenegro]]. {{citation needed|date=May 2012}}. He is also a Public Speaker on subject of Team Work and Team Efficiency working closely with many companies in Spain and other European countries. He is also a co-founder of [https://www.badaisinternational.com BADAIS INTERNATIONAL] a successful flower wholesale business in London UK.

His younger brother, [[Boban Savović|Boban]], is also a retired basketball player and an assistant coach of [[JL Bourg Basket]] of PRO A French premiere basketball league.

After some years working in [[CB Bilbao Berri|Bilbao Basket]] he became the president of the club in December 2010 until he left the club in the summer of 2017. He held a position as a CEO of [[Basket Zaragoza|Basket Zaragoza 2002 S.A.D]]. professional basketball club in Spain from 2017 - 2019. From 2019 to 2021 he was employed one more time as a CEO of [[Bilbao Basket|CD Basket Bilbao Berri S.A.D.]]

In November 2021 he joined a team of Fintech company [[BRYDG CAPITAL]] in [[London]] as a Business Development Manager.
